_method_limits.works_well: English rap over separated vocal stem. 4/4 IDs so far (ian 3.5, ASAP Ferg Demons, Travis Scott NO BYSTANDERS, Wiz Khalifa Pittsburgh Sound).
_method_limits.fails: Indian-language vocals. Forced-language Whisper (medium model, pa/hi/ta/te/sa) produced ZERO usable output on kuthu and bharatanatyam stems, and nothing on the Punjabi bhangra hooks. Causes: sung melisma vs speech models, pitch/tempo shifting by the DJ, heavy layering, and Punjabi being poorly represented in training data.
_method_limits.implication: Automated ID covers the English/western half of a fusion mix only. The desi half - which is the half that defines the style - needs user knowledge or DJ tracklists. Plan accordingly: ask DJs for tracklists, and treat user-supplied IDs as the primary source for desi material.

_dj_tags._comment: DJ tags are spoken signatures. First one captured 2026-08-02. Note the SETUP technique: DJs lead into their tag with a recognizable sample whose lyric primes the name.

KEV7N.text: Guess who's back? Oh my god, I'm really Kevin 7 on the track
KEV7N.setup: 'Guess who's back' = Eminem 'Without Me' hook, used as a lead-in before the tag lands
KEV7N.placement: inside the closing segment, ~23s before the mix ends
KEV7N.formula: '<name> on the track' — same construction as VC's 'VC on the track'

Bassdoctor.text: Is there a doctor in the house?
Bassdoctor.note: This IS the tag itself, not a setup line. Correction from my earlier guess (2026-08-02) - user confirmed. Bassdoctor's tag is a question rather than a '<name> on the track' statement.
Bassdoctor.formula: indirect/pun tag - names the DJ by implication ('doctor') without stating the handle

_tag_formulas._comment: Two axes: WHAT is said (lyrical formula) and HOW it is delivered (production treatment). User-supplied 2026-08-02.

lyrical_formula.direct_statement: '<name> on the track' — VC ('VC on the track'), KEV7N ('I'm really Kevin 7 on the track'). May be primed by a recognizable sample first (KEV7N uses Eminem 'Guess who's back').
lyrical_formula.indirect_pun: Bassdoctor — 'Is there a doctor in the house?'. Names the DJ by implication; handle never spoken.
lyrical_formula.bare_name: Loka — literally just the word 'Loka' spoken.

_tag_formulas.why_detection_failed: Whisper found only 2 of 13 known tags. The delivery treatments explain it: whispered vocals fall below the model's speech threshold, pitched-up/autotuned voices are out of distribution for speech models, and bare one-word names ('Loka') carry no linguistic context to anchor a decode. The tags we DID catch (KEV7N, Bassdoctor) are both full conversational sentences in a normal register. => Automated tag detection will systematically miss the stylized tags; these need the user's ear or a different approach (e.g. audio-fingerprint matching a known tag clip across mixes).
